descriptions: the one Brahman qualified by sentient and insentient beings as its body (cid-acid-viśiṣṭa)
opposed to all that is evil (akhila-heya-pratyanīka) and the sole abode of infinite auspicious qualities (kalyāṇaika-tāna) — the twofold mark (ubhaya-liṅga)
satyam jñānam anantam: real, knowledge, infinite — each word naming a quality of one Brahman, not an attributeless essence
material and efficient cause of the world: in pralaya Brahman has souls and matter as a subtle body; in creation, as a gross body
present in five forms: para, vyūha, vibhava, antaryāmin, arcā
negations: 'neti neti' (BĀU 2.3.6) denies only the limit 'so much' of what was described, not Brahman's qualities
'nirguṇa' denies the defective qualities born of prakṛti, not the auspicious qualities
Brahman is not touched by the changes and imperfections of its body
relation_to_self: The individual self (jīva) is a real, eternal, atomic knower that is a mode (prakāra) and body of Brahman, its servant (śeṣa), wholly dependent (paratantra), never identical with it and never lost in it, even in liberation.
relation_to_world: The world is real; it is the body of Brahman, transformed from subtle to gross in creation while Brahman as its self remains unchanged and unaffected.
caveat: The tradition affirms one ultimate but rejects any reading of 'one truth' as an attributeless or merely impersonal reality: the one is the personal Nārāyaṇa with Śrī, and souls and world remain real and distinct as his body. It rejects Advaita's identity of self and Brahman and the unreality of the world, and would reject a reconciliation that makes Nārāyaṇa one name among equals for a nameless absolute.

names.name: Śrīman Nārāyaṇa (the divine couple, Śrī and Nārāyaṇa)

descriptions: as in Viśiṣṭādvaita generally; with the emphasis that Śrī, all-pervading like Viṣṇu, shares his supremacy and is, with him, the means and the goal (the divine pair, mithuna, is the object of surrender)
relation_to_self: The soul is the servant of the divine couple; it must, by the Lord's grace, perform surrender as the means.
relation_to_world: As for Viśiṣṭādvaita: the world is the real body of the Lord.
caveat: Same caveat as ult:visistadvaita; in addition the Vaṭakalai insist that Śrī is not of the rank of souls.

descriptions: as in Viśiṣṭādvaita generally; with the emphasis that the Lord himself is the already-accomplished means (siddhopāya) whose grace is causeless, who relishes even his devotees' faults, and to whom Śrī, ever inseparable, mediates
relation_to_self: The soul's essence is to belong wholly to the Lord (ananyārha-śeṣatva) and to be dependent (pāratantrya); it brings nothing of its own to its salvation.
relation_to_world: As for Viśiṣṭādvaita: the world is the real body of the Lord.
caveat: Same caveat as ult:visistadvaita; in addition the Teṅkalai reject any view that the soul's own act contributes to its salvation.
